messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — HIGH severity — network egress errors observed in us-east-1a (multiple hosts). Alerts: edge-proxy 5xx > 10% , api-gateway increased latency, some healthchecks failing. Paging shreya (oncall).

shreya (oncall): I’m awake, joining. Looking at Cloud provider console now. Anyone see DNS anomalies?

dmitri (sre): seeing TCP RST spikes from us-east-1a -> transit. Traceroutes from our egress show next-hop blackhole intermittently.

lucas (infra): Confirming. Cloud provider status shows a networking incident in us-east-1 (partial AZ networking degradation). Link: https://status.examplecloud.com/incidents/8452 : "ToT" flap on AZ switching fabric.

shreya (oncall): Ok — customer impact: Hosted API regional latency spikes and a subset of requests returning 502/504. Dedicated clusters in the same AZ showing degraded throughput but not full outage. Starting quick assessment.

amy (eng): Noted that some streaming sessions are failing mid-stream. Rolling back a canary won't help if egress path is flaky.

shreya (oncall): Quick mitigation plan proposal: 1) Pause draining in us-east-1a, avoid creating extra connection churn. 2) Shift traffic away from affected AZ via traffic-shift routing (weighted regional DNS fallback + route priority). 3) If DNS TTL blocks speed, use our edge-router config to reweight at the traffic-router layer.

dmitri (sre): Agreed. I can push a policy to traffic-router to shift 70% off us-east-1a to us-east-1b and 30% to us-west-2. Doing gradual ramp for 10m. Will monitor error budget.

lucas (infra): Before shifting: set pinning exemptions for Dedicated customers (don't break reserved capacity). I'll annotate the routing change with the customer list.

incident-bot: ACTION — dmitri (sre) added a runbook step: traffic-router apply-weight us-east-1a=0.3 us-east-1b=0.55 us-west-2=0.15 (dry-run=false).

shreya (oncall): Executing now. dmitri, paste the command output when done.

dmitri (sre): ran command:
```
traffic-router apply-weight --from us-east-1a --to us-east-1b=0.55,us-west-2=0.15 --reason "az-a network flap" --ticket 8472
Applied change id: change-2026-03-12-01
Status: rolling (10m ramp)
```

shreya (oncall): Early results: 502 rate dropped from 12% -> 3% in 5m. Latency median improved by ~120ms for affected flows. Streaming failures still present for long-lived kv-cache sessions.

amy (eng): Finding root cause for streaming fallback — kv-cache connections in us-east-1a are failing on session reattach. Might be stateful connections pinned to specific fabric. Suggest enabling session-proxy fallback to allow reconnect to new AZ.

dmitri (sre): Enabling session-proxy fallback (10% traffic) to validate. Command:
```
service-config set session-proxy.fallback=true --scope region:us-east-1 --pct 10
```
Applied, monitoring metrics.

shreya (oncall): Also, DNS: provider seems to have queued some failover record updates — TTLs are high (60s) but propagation to some CDNs delayed. For immediate routing control, rely on traffic-router (already done). Opening a support case with DNS provider: SR#DNS-5532.

customer-success-bot: Notifying CS: A subset of customers on us-east-1 may experience degraded latency and intermittent errors. CS owners: @kate and @omar. Template sent.

sre-lead: Good playbook so far. Two asks: 1) prepare customer impact list and quantify RPS impacted; 2) plan for draining us-east-1a only after provider confirms fabric stable. Do not drain blindly — that'll create more connection churn.

lucas (infra): RPS impacted ~8% of global (primarily model-inference auth flows). Dedicated reserved clusters unaffected unless pinned to the AZ — those we will honor. Compiling list: 
- customers: alpha-ads, beta-saas (partial)
- endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/stream
Estimated at-risk requests: ~12k/min at peak.

shreya (oncall): Handoff: I need to step off for 30m to handle pager consolidation (secondary on-call will take). dmitri, you’re primary now for mitigation. Handoff summary below.
```
Handoff summary (shreya -> dmitri):
- AZ us-east-1a networking fabric degraded per provider
- Traffic-router reweight applied: change-2026-03-12-01
- session-proxy fallback enabled 10% to test
- DNS provider case SR#DNS-5532 opened
- CS notified for impacted customers
- Observed: 502s down to 3% after reweight; streaming failures persist
```

shreya (oncall): @dmitri take it, I’ll be reachable via DM if needed. :thumbsup:

dmitri (sre): Taking over. Next steps: increase traffic shift to 85% off us-east-1a if error budget stays stable for 15m, keep session-proxy fallback ramping to 50% if it helps repro attach failures, coordinate with provider. Also prepping incident page for external comms.

amy (eng): If session-proxy fallback helps, we can roll a fast patch to reduce connection pin duration for future mitigation. Will stand by.

incident-bot: UPDATE — provider resolved partial fabric issue at 1768766500 (provider message: "some networking paths restored"). However, provider warns about potential residual intermittent routing discrepancies.

dmitri (sre): Provider update acknowledged. We will keep shifts for 30m and then consider gentle reinstate once metrics stable.

lucas (infra): Reminder: Do not perform full AZ drain until provider gives green and we have warm capacity in other AZs for dedicated workloads.

customer-success-bot: CS update: initial message sent to impacted customer contacts with mitigation summary and ETA for remediation.

shreya (oncall): Back online — thanks team. Anything urgent?

dmitri (sre): All good here. Error rates stable ~<2.5% after ramp. Session fallback reduced streaming failures by ~60% at 50% rollout. Planning to start slow reinstate: set us-east-1a weight to 0.6 in 20m and monitor.

sre-lead: After incident: we need a postmortem covering: TTL/route controls, session pinning anti-pattern, and an automated path to route around flaky fabric without manual DNS pushes. Assign owners.

shreya (oncall): Creating incident ticket INC-2026-8472 and assigning PM/ENG owners for repro and followup. Thanks everyone.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — status: degraded->stabilized at 1768766899. Follow-up tasks assigned to incident ticket INC-2026-8472. Postmortem due in 72h. :white_check_mark:

luccas (typo-intentional): noted for retro.
